p.src: Now Tang Long said to the assembled chiefs, “My family has made its living forging weapons for generations. Through his skill in that craft, my late father won the favor of the old Military Commissioner and was appointed commander of a stockade at Yan’an. In the former dynasty, victories were once won with these ‘chain-linked armored horses.’ To break such a formation, one must use hooked sickle spears. I have the design handed down in my family, so if they are wanted, I can begin forging them at once. Though I know how to forge them, I do not know how to wield them. For someone who can wield one, there is none but my elder cousin on my father’s sister’s side. He alone is an instructor in the hooked sickle spear method. It is an art passed down in his family and never taught to outsiders. Whether mounted or on foot, it has its prescribed methods; when he truly sets it in motion, he appears and vanishes like a spirit!” Before he had finished, Lin Chong asked, “Can you mean Xu Ning, presently an instructor of the Imperial Golden Spear Guard?” Tang Long replied, “That is the man.” Lin Chong said, “I had forgotten him until you mentioned him. Xu Ning’s golden spear and hooked sickle spear techniques truly stand unrivaled beneath Heaven. When I was in the capital, we met often and matched our martial skills; each respected and cherished the other. But how can we persuade him to come up the mountain?”

p.src: Tang Long said, “Xu Ning possesses a peerless treasure bequeathed by his forebears, the heirloom that guards his house. In those days, when I accompanied my late father, the stockade commander, to the Eastern Capital to visit my aunt, I saw it many times. It is a suit of gold-ringed armor fashioned with wild-goose-feather scales. When worn, the armor is both light and secure, and blades, swords, arrows, and bolts cannot readily pierce it. Everyone calls it ‘Peer of the Tang Lion.’ Many noble young gentlemen have asked merely to see it, but he will not casually show it to anyone. That armor is as dear to him as his life. It is kept in a leather case and hung directly from a beam in his bedchamber. If we can first contrive to obtain that armor, he will have no choice but to come here.”

p.src: Wu Yong said, “If that is so, what difficulty can there be? We have a master of such work among our brothers here. This time, Flea on a Drum Shi Qian must make the journey.” Shi Qian immediately replied, “I fear only that the thing may not be there. If it truly is, I shall get it, whatever it takes.” Tang Long said, “If you steal the armor, I guarantee that I shall lure him up the mountain.”

p.src: Song Jiang asked, “How will you lure him up the mountain?” Tang Long whispered several sentences into Song Jiang’s ear. Song Jiang laughed and said, “A splendid plan!” Scholar Wu said, “We shall need three more men to make the journey to the Eastern Capital with them. One is to buy fireworks, medicinal ingredients, and the materials needed for cannon charges in the capital; the other two are to bring Commander Ling’s family here.” At this, Peng Qi rose and petitioned, “If someone could go to Yingzhou and bring my family up the mountain, I would be deeply indebted for such kindness.” Song Jiang said at once, “Have no fear, Training Commissioner. I ask you both to write letters, and I shall send men myself.” He summoned Yang Lin and ordered him to take silver, gold, and the letter, lead attendants to Yingzhou, and fetch General Peng Qi’s family. Xue Yong was to disguise himself as an itinerant staff fighter and medicine seller and go to the Eastern Capital to fetch Commander Ling’s family. Li Yun was to disguise himself as a traveling merchant and also go to the Eastern Capital to purchase fireworks, medicinal ingredients, and other supplies. Yue He was to travel with Tang Long and also accompany Xue Yong on the journey. Meanwhile, they first sent Shi Qian down the mountain. Afterward, Tang Long was told to forge a hooked sickle spear as a model, while Lei Heng was appointed to direct and supervise the work, for Lei Heng’s forebears had also been blacksmiths. To resume: Tang Long forged a model hooked sickle spear, and the weaponsmiths in the stronghold were ordered to copy it, under Lei Heng’s direction and supervision. No more need be said of that. The main stronghold prepared a farewell feast, after which Yang Lin, Xue Yong, Li Yun, Yue He, and Tang Long took their leave and descended the mountain. The next day, Dai Zong too was sent down the mountain to go back and forth gathering news. The full tale of these events cannot be told at once.

p.src: For now, let us tell how Shi Qian left Liangshan Marsh with concealed weapons and all manner of equipment hidden about him, traveled steadily on to the Eastern Capital, and took lodging at an inn. The next day he entered the city and asked where Xu Ning, instructor of the Imperial Golden Spear Guard, lived. Someone directed him: “Enter the Ban Gate; it is the fifth house on the east side, the one with the black-cornered doorway.” Shi Qian turned into the Ban Gate and first examined the front entrance; then he circled around and surveyed the rear entrance. There he saw a long stretch of high wall; beyond it could be seen two small, elegant upper rooms, with a slanting support post to one side. After studying it for a while, Shi Qian went into the neighborhood and asked, “Is Instructor Xu at home?” A man replied, “I expect he is still on duty within the palace and has not returned.” Shi Qian asked again, “Do you know when he will return?” The man replied, “Not until evening. At the fifth watch he leaves again to join his unit in the palace.” Shi Qian thanked him for the information and returned to the inn. He collected his equipment, concealed it about his person, and instructed the waiter, “I shall most likely not return tonight. Please look after my room.” The waiter said, “Go without worry. Nothing will go amiss.”

p.src: Shi Qian entered the city again, bought himself some supper, and after eating it made his way to the Gold-Lance Guard quarters and Xu Ning's home. Looking all around, he could find nowhere suitable to hide. When darkness had nearly fallen, Shi Qian slipped inside the guard-quarter gate. It was a wintry night, cold and moonless. Behind the shrine of the local earth god, Shi Qian saw a great cypress. Gripping its trunk between his legs, he climbed steadily to the crown and sat astride a branch. Peering out in silence, he saw Xu Ning return and go into his house. Then he saw two men emerge from the quarters carrying lanterns. They shut the gate, secured it with a lock, and each went home. Before long, the curfew drum sounded from the watchtower, marking the first watch. Cold clouds dimmed the stars; scattered dew turned gradually to whitening frost. When Shi Qian saw that all was silent in the quarters, he slid down the tree, stole around to Xu Ning's back gate, and scaled the wall without the least effort. Looking within, he found a small courtyard. Crouching outside the kitchen, Shi Qian peered in. A lamp still burned there, and two maidservants had not yet finished tidying up. Shi Qian climbed a slanting support to the bargeboard and flattened himself against it. Peering into the upper floor, he saw Xu Ning the Gold-Lance Master and his wife seated together warming themselves by the brazier, with a child of six or seven in Xu Ning's arms. Looking into the bedchamber, Shi Qian saw that a large leather case was indeed fastened to a beam. A bow and arrows and a saber hung by the chamber door. Garments of various kinds hung on a clothes rack. Xu Ning called out, “Meixiang, come and fold my clothes.” One of the maidservants below came upstairs. On the side table she first folded a purple embroidered round-collared robe, then an official-green lined jacket, together with multicolored embroidered gaiters, a bright brocade neckcloth, a red-and-green cord, and a bundle containing a handkerchief. In a small yellow cloth she separately wrapped a gold belt decorated with paired otter tails and lychee motifs, placed that in the bundle as well, and set the whole thing atop the warming basket. Shi Qian took careful note of everything. Sometime after the second watch, Xu Ning prepared for bed, and his wife asked, “Are you reporting for duty tomorrow?” Xu Ning said, “Tomorrow the Son of Heaven is proceeding to Longfu Palace. I must rise early and attend him at the fifth watch.” Hearing this, his wife instructed Meixiang, “The master must rise at the fifth watch tomorrow and go out with his unit. Rise at the fourth watch, heat water, and prepare some refreshments.” Shi Qian thought to himself, “Plainly, that leather case on the beam is the one containing the armor. It would be best if I made my move at midnight. But if an uproar breaks out and I cannot leave the city tomorrow, will that not ruin the greater undertaking? …I shall wait until the fifth watch; that will not be too late.”

p.src: He heard Xu Ning and his wife retire to bed, while the two maidservants spread their bedding outside the chamber door. A bowl-lamp remained alight on the table inside. All five of them fell asleep. The two maidservants, worn out after attending their masters all day, also slept soundly. Shi Qian slid down, took a reed tube from his person, and blew once through a gap in the window lattice. The bowl-lamp immediately went out. Near the fourth watch, Xu Ning arose and called the maidservants to get up and heat water. The two serving girls rose from their sleep. Seeing that the room was dark, they cried, “Oh! The lamp has gone out tonight!” Xu Ning said, “Why do you not go to the back and fetch a light? What are you waiting for?” One maid opened the upstairs door and clattered down the ladder-stairs. Hearing her, Shi Qian slid straight down the pillar and crouched in the shadows beside the back gate. When he heard the maid open the back door and go out to unlock the courtyard gate, Shi Qian slipped into the kitchen and pressed himself beneath the kitchen table. The maid returned with a flame, shut the gate again, and came to kindle the kitchen fire. The other serving girl also rose, lit a charcoal brazier, and carried it upstairs. After some time the water boiled. They carried up a basin, and when Xu Ning had washed, he ordered them to warm and bring him some wine. The maid took up meat and steamed cakes. When Xu Ning had finished eating, he told her to give food to the attendants on duty outside. Shi Qian heard Xu Ning come downstairs, summon his attendant to eat, then shoulder his bundle, take up the golden lance, and leave the house. The two maids lit lamps and escorted Xu Ning out. Shi Qian emerged from beneath the kitchen table, went upstairs, climbed straight along the side to the beam, and lay flat upon it. The two maidservants barred the doors once more, extinguished the lamps, went upstairs, undressed, and fell straight into bed.

p.src: When Shi Qian heard that the two maids were asleep, he aimed his reed tube from the beam and blew at the lamp, which immediately went out again. Shi Qian quietly untied the leather case from the beam. Just as he was about to descend, Xu Ning's wife awoke, heard a noise, and called to the maid, “What is making that sound on the beam?” Shi Qian mimicked the squeak of a rat. The maid replied, “My lady, can you not hear that it is rats squeaking? They are fighting, which is why they make such a noise.” Taking his cue, Shi Qian imitated rats fighting and slid down. He quietly opened the upstairs door, gently shouldered the leather case, descended the ladder-stairs, and opened the doors one after another from within until he reached the outer gate and came to the guard-quarter entrance. Men reporting for duty had already begun to leave, so the lock had been opened at the fourth watch. With the leather case in hand, Shi Qian mingled with the crowd and slipped out amid the bustle. Without pausing for breath, he ran beyond the city to the inn. Dawn had not yet broken. He knocked open the inn door, fetched his luggage from his room, bound it into a shoulder load, and took it up. After settling the room charge, he left the inn and headed east.

p.src: Only after traveling forty li did he stop at an eating house, light the cooking fire, and prepare a meal. Just then another man came bustling in. When Shi Qian looked, it was none other than Dai Zong, the “Magic Traveler.” Seeing that Shi Qian had secured the object, Dai Zong exchanged a few quiet words with him and said, “I shall take the armor back to the stronghold first. You and Tang Long may follow at your leisure.” Shi Qian opened the leather case, took out the suit of wild-goose-feather mail, and wrapped it into a bundle. Dai Zong fastened it to his body, left the shop, invoked his magic-traveling art, and sped away toward Liangshan Marsh.

p.src: Shi Qian conspicuously tied the empty leather case to his load. After eating, he paid for the use of the fire, shouldered his burden, and left the shop. Twenty li farther on, he met Tang Long, and the two entered a tavern to confer. Tang Long said, “Follow this road exactly as I tell you. Whenever you pass a tavern, eating house, or inn and see a white chalk circle on its door, go inside, buy wine and meat, and eat. If it is an inn, stay the night there, and deliberately place this leather case where everyone can see it. Then wait for me one day's journey from here.” Shi Qian departed according to the plan. Tang Long leisurely drank wine for a while, then made his way toward the Eastern Capital.

p.src: Now at daybreak in Xu Ning’s house, the two maidservants arose and saw that the upstairs door stood open; below, neither the inner gate nor the main gate was shut. They hurriedly inspected the house and found every article still there. Going upstairs, they told their mistress, “We do not know how all the doors came to be open, yet nothing has been lost.” His wife said, “During the fifth watch I heard a noise in the rafters, and you said it was rats fighting. Go and see whether anything has happened to that leather case.” The two maids looked and cried out in dismay, “The leather case has vanished—we do not know where!” Hearing this, his wife sprang up in alarm and said, “Quickly ask someone to go to Longfu Palace and tell the master. Have him return early and help search for it!” The maids urgently found people to carry word to Xu Ning at Longfu Palace, asking three or four in succession, but all returned saying, “The Imperial Golden-Lance Guard has accompanied His Majesty into the inner park. Outside, the imperial troops are guarding every approach. Who could possibly get in? You will simply have to wait until he returns on his own.” Xu Ning’s wife and the two maids were like ants on a hot pan, with nowhere to turn. They could neither eat nor drink and were thrown into complete confusion.

p.src: Not until dusk did Xu Ning remove his official robe and insignia. Having an attendant carry his golden lance behind him, he went straight home. When he reached the guard-quarter gate, a neighbor said, “Your house was robbed. Your wife has been waiting for you, Inspector, but you did not return.” Xu Ning was startled and hurried home. The two maids met him at the door and said, “After you went out during the fifth watch, Master, a thief slipped inside and stole only the leather case upon the beam.” When Xu Ning heard this, he groaned again and again, the cries rolling up from the depths of his belly and straight out of his mouth. His wife said, “We truly do not know when that thief slipped into the house.” Xu Ning said, “Nothing else matters, but that suit of wild-goose-feather armor is a treasure handed down through four generations of my family and had never once been lost. Grand Commandant Wang ‘the Dandy’ once offered me thirty thousand strings of cash for it, but I could not bear to sell it to him. Fearing I might need it one day before the armies or amid the battle lines, and dreading the slightest mishap, I fastened it to the beam. Many people asked to see it, but I always claimed I no longer had it. If I make an outcry now, I shall only invite ridicule. Yet it is truly gone—what am I to do?” Xu Ning could not sleep all night and reflected, “I wonder what sort of person stole it! It must have been someone who knew about this armor of mine.” His wife considered and said, “Could the thief already have been hiding in the house last night when we put out the lamp? Someone must have coveted your armor but failed to buy it even with money, and therefore sent this master thief to steal it. You should ask people to investigate it quietly, then decide what to do. For now, do not beat the grass and startle the snake.” Xu Ning listened to her and, when day broke, arose and sat at home brooding. He was like this:

p.src: Hearing this, Xu Ning hurriedly changed into hemp sandals, fastened on his saber, took up a quarterstaff-blade, and left by the eastern outer gate with Tang Long. Lengthening their stride, they hurried on after the thief. Ahead they saw an inn marked by a white circle on its wall. Tang Long said, “Let us have a bowl of wine before we go on, and ask about him here while we are at it.” Tang Long entered and sat down, then asked, “Innkeeper, may I ask whether a sharp-eyed, thin, dark-complexioned fellow passed this way carrying a red sheepskin case?” The innkeeper replied, “Last night there was indeed just such a man, carrying a red sheepskin case, who passed this way. He seemed to have hurt his leg in a fall and could only hobble along one step at a time.” Tang Long said, “Brother, what do you make of that?” Xu Ning heard him but could not utter a word.

p.src: The two hurriedly paid for the wine and went out to continue their pursuit. Farther on they came to another inn with a white circle painted on its wall. Tang Long stopped and said, “Brother, I can walk no farther. Let us rest at this inn for now. We shall set out early tomorrow and catch up with him.” Xu Ning said, “But I hold an official post. If I fail to answer roll call, the authorities will surely hold me to account. What am I to do?” Tang Long replied, “You need not worry about that, elder brother. My sister-in-law will surely find some excuse for you.” That evening, when they made inquiries at the inn, a waiter replied, “Last night a sharp-eyed, thin, dark-complexioned fellow stayed here. He slept until nearly noon today before leaving. All he asked about was the road to Shandong.” Tang Long said, “Then we can catch him. If we rise at the fourth watch tomorrow, we are certain to overtake him. Once we seize the scoundrel, we shall learn where the armor is.” The two rested that night. The next day they rose at the fourth watch, left the inn, and continued steadily in pursuit. Whenever Tang Long saw a whitewashed circle on a wall, he would stop on the pretext of buying wine and food and ask about the road; everywhere they heard the same story. Xu Ning was desperate to recover his suit of armor and did nothing but follow Tang Long onward in pursuit. As dusk was once again approaching, they saw an old temple ahead. Beneath a tree before it, Shi Qian had set down his carrying pole and was sitting on the ground. When Tang Long saw him, he cried, “Excellent! Is that not the case in which you kept your armor, brother, there beneath the tree?” At the sight, Xu Ning rushed forward, seized Shi Qian, and shouted, “You have monstrous audacity, scoundrel! How dare you steal my suit of armor!” Shi Qian said, “Wait, wait! Do not shout! Yes, I stole your armor. What do you intend to do about it now?” Xu Ning roared, “You insolent beast! You have the gall to ask what I mean to do!” Shi Qian said, “First look inside the case and see whether the armor is there.” Tang Long opened the case and looked, but it was empty. Xu Ning demanded, “Where have you taken my armor, scoundrel?” Shi Qian said, “Hear me out. My humble name is Zhang, I am the eldest son, and I come from Tai'an Prefecture. A wealthy man in our prefecture wished to cultivate the acquaintance of the Senior Military Commissioner. He knew your family possessed this suit of wild-goose-feather chain armor and would not sell it. So he specially sent me and another man, Li San, to steal it from your house, promising us ten thousand strings of cash. But I fell from a pillar in your house and wrenched my leg, so I could not walk properly. I sent Li San ahead with the armor, leaving me here with only the empty case. If you mean to take me before the authorities, I shall simply stake my life on it. Even if you beat me to death, I shall confess nothing, and you may abandon all hope of making me name my accomplice. But if you are willing to spare me a case before the authorities, I shall go with you, recover the armor, and return it to you.” Xu Ning hesitated for a long while, unable to decide. Tang Long said, “Brother, there is no fear of his flying away! Let us simply go with him to recover the armor! If the armor is not there, we can always lodge a complaint with the local authorities.” Xu Ning said, “What you say is right, brother.” The three urged one another onward and went to lodge at another inn. Xu Ning and Tang Long kept Shi Qian under guard and slept in the same room with him. In truth, Shi Qian had deliberately bound some strips of silk around his leg and merely pretended to have sprained it. Seeing that he was still unable to walk properly, Xu Ning maintained only half the vigilance he otherwise would have shown. The three rested for another night and set out early the next morning. All along the way, Shi Qian bought them wine and meat and spoke apologetically to placate them. Thus they traveled for another day.

p.src: The next day, as they traveled, Xu Ning grew anxious, not knowing whether the armor was truly there or not. As they went on, they saw three or four pack animals by the roadside pulling an empty cart. One man drove it from behind, while a traveler walking beside it caught sight of Tang Long and immediately bowed low. Tang Long asked, “Brother, what brings you here?” The man replied, “I have finished my business in Zhengzhou and am returning to Tai'an Prefecture.” Tang Long said, “Excellent. The three of us would like a ride, for we too are bound for Tai'an Prefecture.” The man said, “Three passengers are nothing; I would not mind even a few more.” Tang Long was delighted and introduced him to Xu Ning. Xu Ning asked, “Who is this man?” Tang Long replied, “When I went to offer incense in Tai'an Prefecture last year, I befriended this brother. His surname is Li and his given name is Rong; he is a man of honor.” Xu Ning said, “In that case, since Zhang Yi can walk no farther, let us all ride in the cart.” They had the driver set the cart in motion. The four men sat in the cart, and Xu Ning asked, “Zhang Yi, tell me the name of that wealthy gentleman.” Pressed beyond endurance, Shi Qian evaded the question again and again, but at last blurted out at random, “He is the renowned Gentleman Guo.” Xu Ning then asked Li Rong, “Is there a Gentleman Guo in your Tai'an Prefecture?” Li Rong replied, “Gentleman Guo of our prefecture is a wealthy man of a leading household. He especially enjoys associating with officials, and keeps many retainers at his gate.” Hearing this, Xu Ning thought, “Since the armor has an owner, there can surely be no trouble.” Moreover, Li Rong talked of spear and staff fighting along the road and sang several songs, and before they knew it another day had passed. Let us waste no more words. When they had drawn within a little over two stages of Liangshan Marsh, Li Rong told the driver to take the gourd and buy some wine and meat, so that they might drink a few cups in the cart. Li Rong took out a dipper, filled it first, and offered it to Xu Ning, who drained it in one draught. When Li Rong called for more wine, the driver pretended that his hand had slipped and spilled the whole gourdful onto the ground. Li Rong cursed the driver and ordered him to buy some more. Presently, saliva ran from the corners of Xu Ning's mouth, and he toppled over in the cart. Who was Li Rong? He was none other than Yue He, the Iron Whistle. The three leapt down from the cart and hurried it straight to the inn of Zhu Gui, the Dry-Land Crocodile. There the men carried Xu Ning aboard a boat, and they all went ashore at Golden Sands Beach. Song Jiang had already received word and came down the mountain with the chieftains to meet them. By then Xu Ning had awakened from the drug, and the men administered an antidote as well. Xu Ning opened his eyes and, seeing the assembled men, was startled. He asked Tang Long, “Brother, why have you tricked me into coming here?” Tang Long said, “Brother, please hear me out. I recently learned that Song Gongming was welcoming heroes from every quarter. Therefore, at Wugang Town I acknowledged the Black Whirlwind Li Kui as my elder brother and came to join this great stronghold. Now Huyan Zhuo has charged our ranks with his chain-armored cavalry, and we have found no way to break it. I proposed the hooked-spear method, but only you, brother, know how to wield it. So we devised this plan: first Shi Qian was sent to steal your armor; then I was to lure you onto the road; and finally Yue He was to impersonate Li Rong and, as we passed the mountain, drug you with knockout wine and invite you up here to take a seat among us.” Xu Ning said, “Brother, you have ruined me!” Song Jiang came forward with a cup and apologized, saying, “At present I, Song Jiang, dwell temporarily by this marsh, awaiting only the court's offer of amnesty, so that I may devote all my loyalty and strength to serving the realm. I would never dare covet wealth, delight in killing, or commit cruel and unrighteous deeds.

Several days later, Dai Zong and Tang Long brought Xu Ning's family up the mountain.

p.src: Xu Ning was startled when he saw his wife arrive and asked how she had managed to come there. His wife replied, “After you left, when you failed to answer the authorities' roll call, I spent some gold, silver, and jewelry and merely claimed that you were ill in bed, so they did not come to summon you. Then Uncle Tang suddenly appeared carrying the wild-goose-plume armor and said, ‘We recovered the armor. But elder brother has fallen ill on the road and is close to dying in an inn. He asks his wife and child to come and see him at once.’ He tricked me into the cart, and since I did not know the way, I traveled on and on until I arrived here.” Xu Ning said, “Brother, all is well now, to be sure. It is only a pity that my suit of armor has been left behind at home.” Tang Long laughed and said, “Brother, I have good news for you. After I sent sister-in-law off in the cart, I turned back, tricked them out of the armor, enticed these two maidservants away, gathered up all the valuables in the house, and brought them here in a shoulder load.” Xu Ning said, “If that is so, we can never return to the Eastern Capital.”

p.src: Tang Long said, “There is one more thing you should know, brother. Halfway here, we encountered a band of travelers. I put on your wild-goose-plume armor, painted my face, gave your name, and robbed them of their belongings. By now the Eastern Capital must already have circulated warrants everywhere for your arrest.” Xu Ning said, “Brother, you have done me no small harm!” Chao Gai and Song Jiang both came to placate him, saying, “Had we not done this, Inspector, how could we ever have persuaded you to remain here?” They immediately assigned them a house and settled Xu Ning's family there. The chieftains then discussed how to defeat the chain-armored cavalry.

p.src: By this time, Lei Heng had finished supervising the manufacture of all the hooked spears. Song Jiang, Wu Yong, and the others invited Xu Ning to instruct the soldiers in the hooked-spear method. Xu Ning said, “I shall now reveal the method without reserve, train the officers and soldiers, and select men who are tall and powerfully built.” All the chieftains gathered in the Hall of Righteous Assembly to watch Xu Ning select the troops and explain the hooked-spear method. And so it came to pass that three thousand armored horsemen would soon be routed, and one hero would shortly submit. How the Golden-Lance Xu Ning demonstrated the hooked-spear method will be told in the next chapter.
